messages.author: 5831f7348c4bca63
messages.subject: Adding interaction terms
parts:
Dear all,

I am trying to test the effect of confounders, for instance age or income (continuous variables) by adding directly to the following model (based on the theory of planned behaviour)

SEMtpbmodel <- '

   # latent variables

A =~ att1 + att2

 SN =~ sn1 + sn2

 PBC =~ pbc1 + pbc2

   # regressions

     INT ~ A + SN + PBC

Should I add, for instance inc (income), to each construct (A, SN, PBC)? Or add to the main regression only: INT ~ A + SN + PBC + inc ?

or do I need to interact with each constructs like this: INT ~ inc*A + inc*SN + inc*PBC 

I look forward to your advice.

Thank you in advance!

Nam

messages.author: 82889e926eb5165e
messages.subject: Re: Adding interaction terms
parts:
Nam

Sadly the answer is "it depends".

If you want to talk in the "common" use of a covariate variable, if you want to make it equivalent to linear regression you add it as a predictor only for the main regression. If you want to control for its effect on all the model, you add it as a predictor for all the factors.
You would add the interactions only if you are interested in the change of slope as a function of the coavriates

As a side not, you cannot add interactions like that in lavaan, there you are labeling the regressions, not adding an interaction. Given that you have latent variables you would have to create a latent interaction factor with double mean center or residual center interaction indicators. Check the indprod() function from semTools for this
